Senses.Explanation: “at / meet the trigger or occasion.” In Chan records the occasion is repeatedly public and interpersonal: one account says that in all his questions and answers he “did not yield when meeting the occasion” (問答，當機不讓); a verse pairs a clear question and a direct answer with “meeting face-to-face on the occasion” (當機覿面). The phrase can introduce a request—“with one phrase meeting the occasion, please speak the teaching” (一句當機請師說法)—or appraise an immediate response. Feiyin Tongrong strikes the staff and says, “freed through on the occasion; it is no other thing” (當機透脫，更非別物). Yuanwu's verse says that buddhas and patriarchs “value what is ready-made when meeting the occasion” (佛祖當機貴見成) and immediately calls for someone to come before the assembly and settle doubt. Thus the corpus bends a general word for apt timing toward the live occasion of encounter, question, answer, and response.
